title: 3D gradient hot-path investigation and ten-hypothesis extension
scope: Steady-state point sampling and SIMD/parallel bulk generation of 16×256×16 and 32×256×32 four-octave 3D fields on .NET 10/x64 AVX2.
question: Can shared 3D kernel changes improve both point and bulk APIs by at least 3% without output changes or material regression, and is additional bulk parallelism needed?

summary.headline: The prior packed-gradient optimization remains retained. Ten additional hypotheses yielded no further retained change: the sole viable candidate did not establish a consistent 3% gain across point and bulk APIs.

items.label: One packed-code gather plus signed terms

hypotheses.claim: Encoding each restricted 3D gradient in one integer removes two of three random gathers.
hypotheses.mechanism: M6/C3: reduce random table traffic from three VGATHERDPS to one VPGATHERDD per gradient
hypotheses.prediction: At least 5% lower median gradient time and complete 3D caller time.
hypotheses.falsification: Less than 5% repeatable gain, changed outputs, or a material control regression.
hypotheses.change: Added GradientCodes3D and integer gather support; GradCoord3 decodes one packed code.
hypotheses.maintainability: One compact lookup representation replaces three parallel float tables in the hot path; generic and AVX2 gather implementations both remain covered.
hypotheses.codeComments: The packed-code layout is documented at its declaration and decode site.
hypotheses.result: Isolated operation improved 42.7%; FullOpts Perlin improved 30.6%; all correctness tests passed.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: Large isolated and complete-caller gains survived controls and output tests; the representation cost is bounded.
risks: AVX2-specific magnitude; software fallback is correctness-tested but not separately benchmarked on ARM/AVX-512 hardware.

hypotheses.claim: Apply packed sign bits directly to coordinates instead of reconstructing coefficients and multiplying.
hypotheses.mechanism: C4: sign-bit XOR and zero-axis selection remove three vector multiplies and recover register pressure.
hypotheses.prediction: Preserve H-001's gather reduction without increasing the OpenSimplex2 frame or code size.
hypotheses.falsification: A larger frame/code body, output mismatch, or loss of caller benefit.
hypotheses.change: Decode gradient signs with FlipSign on xd/yd/zd and select only the zero component.
hypotheses.maintainability: The sign decoding is localized within GradCoord3 and avoids redundant coefficient construction.
hypotheses.codeComments: The packed-code decode comment explains the sign and zero-axis fields.
hypotheses.result: Final FullOpts body is 2,290 bytes with a 0x4A0 frame versus baseline 2,294 bytes/0x4A0; six float gathers became two integer gathers per Sample3 call.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: Preserved the gather benefit while keeping generated code size and frame stable.

hypotheses.claim: Software spill-and-index gathers may beat AVX2 hardware gather on this CPU.
hypotheses.mechanism: M6/C3: replace high-latency VGATHERDPS with independent scalar loads.
hypotheses.prediction: Lower GatherStrategy time than the shipped AVX2 path.
hypotheses.falsification: Software gather is slower beyond noise.
hypotheses.change: No library change; compared existing VectorOps.GatherSoftware control.
hypotheses.maintainability: Benchmark-only comparison; no production-code burden was incurred.
hypotheses.codeComments: No library implementation or comment was added.
hypotheses.result: Software gather was 934.0 µs versus 356.9 µs for hardware gather (2.62× slower).
hypotheses.decisionRationale: The measured software path is substantially slower on the target AVX2 host.

hypotheses.claim: Hoisting coordinate broadcasts from GridFill.Rows3 could materially improve the caller.
hypotheses.mechanism: C1/R2: remove repeated invariant vector construction.
hypotheses.falsification: Grid traversal has less than 5% exclusive contribution.
hypotheses.result: GridFill.Rows3 measured 1.60% exclusive CPU baseline; its Amdahl ceiling is below the acceptance threshold.

hypotheses.claim: Manual unrolling of the two-lattice loop could remove loop control.
hypotheses.mechanism: C2: remove one predictable back-edge branch.
hypotheses.falsification: The removable control is negligible relative to duplicated kernel code.
hypotheses.result: Only one CMP/JNE controls a 2,294-byte body; duplicating it would approximately double hot code to remove one predictable branch.

hypotheses.claim: Kernel dispatch is a material cost inside the representative caller.
hypotheses.mechanism: R1/R2: specialize or reorder NoisePipeline.Single3 dispatch.
hypotheses.prediction: Dispatch contributes at least 5% exclusive CPU.
hypotheses.falsification: Measured exclusive contribution below 5% with direct kernel attribution dominant.
hypotheses.result: NoisePipeline.Single3 was 1.70% exclusive baseline; kernel work dominated.

hypotheses.claim: The packed code should also replace GradCoordDual3's float gathers.
hypotheses.mechanism: M6/C4: reuse the retained encoding in domain-warp dual gradients.
hypotheses.falsification: No production caller reaches GradCoordDual3 in the current repository.
hypotheses.result: Repository call-graph search found only the definition; changing an uncalled path would not affect the measured workload.

hypotheses.claim: Bounds-check removal or raw-pointer traversal can materially improve the fill.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 5% complete-caller reduction and visible range-check failure edges.
hypotheses.falsification: Existing stores and gathers already use proven byrefs/pointers and the traversal is below 5% exclusive CPU.
hypotheses.result: The hot lookup already lowers to hardware gather from a GC-tracked table base and the destination store uses Unsafe.WriteUnaligned under a proven loop bound.

hypotheses.claim: Replace initial sign conversion and multiplication by absolute value in OpenSimplex2 Sample3.
hypotheses.mechanism: C4/C3: remove three integer-to-float conversions and three vector multiplies after the nearest-lattice signs are known.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower complete point and bulk time with unchanged output and no material parallel regression.
hypotheses.falsification: Any output difference, less than 3% repeatable complete-API gain, or a material regression in parallel bulk.
hypotheses.change: Temporarily replaced three expressions with TOps.Abs; reverted after the full-API experiments remained confounded.
hypotheses.maintainability: Three local expressions simplify; no new API or state is required. The candidate was reverted pending decisive complete-API timing.
hypotheses.codeComments: No comment was needed for the self-explanatory absolute-value expressions; the source variant is preserved as a patch.
hypotheses.result: Isolated SIMD mechanism improved 403.5→147.2 µs/100k vectors. Point API improved about 3–5% in quiet rounds; SIMD bulk and parallel bulk were multimodal, with a 5–17% apparent parallel regression in some rounds. No adoption claim is justified.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: The revised 3% criterion is not established consistently across the complete point and bulk APIs; especially parallel outcomes conflict.
risks: Uncoordinated host load caused bimodal complete-fill timings. The temporary change has been reverted.

hypotheses.claim: Flip the sign bit instead of converting an integer sign and multiplying the second-lattice offset.
hypotheses.mechanism: C4: replace conversion and multiply with an XOR sign operation.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower isolated signed-offset cost before complete-API promotion.
hypotheses.falsification: The isolated effect is within dispersion or exceptional sign values change results.
hypotheses.maintainability: A local sign-bit operation would be simple, but exceptional-sign handling would add complexity.
hypotheses.codeComments: No production comment was added because the candidate was not promoted.
hypotheses.result: 112.4 versus 113.5 µs/100k vectors (about 1%); standard deviations 6.1 and 4.5 µs. The isolated effect is below the revised threshold and not distinguishable from noise.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: The isolated gain is below 3% and within dispersion, so complete-API promotion is unwarranted.
risks: Non-finite coordinates can produce integer signs other than ±1; XOR would not equal multiplication then.

hypotheses.claim: Construct selected face-neighbor ±1 offsets by sign-bit XOR instead of integer-to-float conversion.
hypotheses.mechanism: C4: remove conversion from the neighbor-coordinate path.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower isolated selected-offset cost.
hypotheses.falsification: The isolated effect is within dispersion or exceptional sign values break equivalence.
hypotheses.maintainability: A local XOR would be simple only if the sign invariant were guaranteed; it is not for exceptional inputs.
hypotheses.codeComments: No production comment was added because the candidate was not promoted.
hypotheses.result: 114.9 versus 117.5 µs/100k vectors (about 2.2%); 4.8–9.5 µs standard deviations. No reproducible 3% gain.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: The isolated result neither reaches 3% nor clears measurement dispersion.
risks: Exceptional signs are not guaranteed to be ±1.

hypotheses.claim: Drop the Y>X comparison from the face-neighbor selection because X was already excluded.
hypotheses.mechanism: C2/C3: remove one vector comparison and mask dependency.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower selection cost while preserving all point and bulk outputs.
hypotheses.falsification: Any coordinate, including NaN, changes selected lattice corner.
hypotheses.change: Benchmark-only three-comparison alternative; no library edit.
hypotheses.maintainability: One fewer comparison would simplify the source, but restoring NaN behavior would erase that simplification.
hypotheses.codeComments: No production comment was added because the candidate is semantically invalid.
hypotheses.result: The finite-input microbenchmark improved 254.1→220.8 µs/100k vectors, but it is not equivalent for NaN. For ax=0.1, ay=NaN, az=0.2, the original selects Z while the candidate selects Y.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: A finite-only gain cannot justify changing the single-sample and bulk exceptional-input contract.
risks: Changing exceptional-input behavior violates the existing scalar/SIMD contract.

hypotheses.claim: Clamp negative attenuation to zero before computing its quartic contribution.
hypotheses.mechanism: C2/C4: replace compare-and-blend after multiplication by a vector Max before multiplication.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower isolated attenuation cost with bit-identical outputs.
hypotheses.falsification: No repeatable gain or any exceptional-input difference.
hypotheses.maintainability: The clamp is local, but any repair for NaN propagation would complicate the kernel.
hypotheses.codeComments: No production comment was added because the candidate is slower and semantically invalid.
hypotheses.result: Candidate mean 123.8 versus 116.1 µs/100k vectors; baseline was bimodal. With negative attenuation and NaN gradient, the original selects zero while the clamped variant propagates NaN.
hypotheses.decisionRationale: The isolated result is slower and the candidate changes exceptional-input outputs.

hypotheses.claim: An explicit AVX2 packed-bitmask path may eliminate generic-vector decode overhead.
hypotheses.mechanism: C3/R2: use AVX2 gather, XOR and blend intrinsics directly in the hot gradient path.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower complete point and bulk time through fewer native instructions.
hypotheses.falsification: The existing generic path already lowers to the same AVX2 instructions.
hypotheses.result: The current path already contains VPGATHERDD, VPCMPEQD, VPAND, VPXOR and VBLENDVPS with no virtual dispatch. A fixed-width rewrite lacks a distinct eliminated operation on this host.
risks: Explicit AVX2 would add a separate ISA path and portability cost.

hypotheses.claim: Prefetching the packed gradient-code table before the gather may hide memory latency.
hypotheses.mechanism: M6/C3: issue prefetch intrinsics ahead of indexed table access.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower complete point and bulk time from fewer demand-load stalls.
hypotheses.falsification: The table is cache resident or the index is unavailable far enough ahead to hide latency.
hypotheses.change: None; inspected table size and dependency order.
hypotheses.result: The entire 64×4-byte table is 256 bytes; the random index is produced immediately before the gather. No miss evidence or independent lookahead exists. Cache residency is probable but was not measured; a prefetch is unjustified without a demonstrated miss mechanism.

hypotheses.claim: A stencil of adjacent samples could reuse lattice work across a spatial block.
hypotheses.mechanism: C1/M7: cache shared lattice gradients or hashes across neighboring grid points.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower complete point and bulk time after cache maintenance costs.
hypotheses.falsification: Point calls lack adjacent-sample context or rotated multi-octave cells provide insufficient reuse.
hypotheses.change: None; inspected point and row-fill call boundaries.
hypotheses.result: GetNoise samples an independent coordinate with no persistent traversal state. A stencil would apply only to a bulk traversal unless a new stateful point API were introduced; it does not meet the required shared point/bulk change.
risks: New persistent cache would change object state, memory cost, and concurrency semantics.

hypotheses.claim: Block-copy repeated output regions instead of evaluating every sample.
hypotheses.mechanism: M7: replace repeated computation with a contiguous copy.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower point and bulk time with exactly equal values.
hypotheses.falsification: Adjacent coordinates do not generally have identical noise outputs.
hypotheses.change: None; inspected coordinate-dependent transforms and the exact-output contract.
hypotheses.result: Each coordinate passes through rotation, multiple octaves and lattice gradients. There is no exact repeated block to copy; approximation or tiling would change outputs, and a single point has no block destination.

hypotheses.claim: Adding worker threads or aligning row partitions removes a material large-fill limit or false-sharing cost.
hypotheses.mechanism: T1/C3: schedule independent row ranges and avoid cross-worker cache-line ownership.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 3% lower large bulk time; point sampling has no independent work within one call.
hypotheses.falsification: Bulk already uses all available workers and sharing is confined to worker boundaries.
hypotheses.change: No algorithm change; corrected the internal comment about possible boundary-line sharing.
hypotheses.result: NoiseGenerator.Fill already selects RowScheduler.Parallel above ParallelThreshold=16384; 65,536-sample OpenSimplex2 fills measured about 3.9 ms SIMD versus 0.5 ms parallel. At most one cache line per adjacent worker range can be shared; no contention hotspot was observed.
risks: Nested parallelism can increase scheduling cost when callers already partition work.

retainedChanges: Represent each of the 64 3D gradients as a five-bit code identifying its zero axis and sign bits.
Add scalar and portable-vector integer gather operations with an AVX2 hardware path and bounded software fallback.
Apply sign bits directly to coordinate terms, eliminating two random gathers and three coefficient multiplies per gradient.
Add a reusable Gradient3DStrategy benchmark and exhaustive table-encoding correctness test.
decisions: H-009 remains unretained. The user accepts a simple 3% gain, but the two point rounds span 2.7–3.4%; bulk and parallel measurements were confounded by uncoordinated host load. Re-run the preserved variant when the host is quiet before adopting it.
correctness: Complete solution tests: 263 passed, 8 GPU-hardware tests skipped by existing environment guards, 0 failed.
The new exhaustive test verifies all 64 packed codes reconstruct all three reference-table components exactly.
Existing compatibility and backend-agreement tests compare scalar/SIMD results to the vendored FastNoiseLite reference across algorithms, rotations, fractals, and coordinates.
Controlled caller checksums were unchanged for OpenSimplex2, Perlin, Value, and Cellular across every baseline/candidate run.
H-009 candidate passed the full solution suite: 263 passed, 8 guarded GPU skips, 0 failed. Point, SIMD bulk and parallel bulk checksums matched baseline for both volume sizes.
H-009 exceptional-input probe compared 207 output bit patterns across scalar point and scalar/SIMD/parallel bulk; baseline and candidate matched exactly.

validityThreats: The host showed material frequency/background-load drift and tier-transition bimodality. Whole-caller conclusions therefore emphasize same-process microbenchmarks, A/B/A repetition, unaffected controls, and FullOpts diagnostics rather than the rejected initial BDN means.
OpenSimplex2 FullOpts candidate repeats differed substantially (1.6% to 23.2% faster); only the conservative repeat is used in its scorecard. Tiered-PGO epoch-2 repeats were 7.4% and 12.0% faster.
Magnitude is established on one Zen 3 AVX2 host. The portable scalar fallback passed correctness tests, but performance on ARM, AVX-512, and non-AVX2 x64 remains unmeasured.
EventPipe sampling attributes heavily inlined work to large callers; percentages locate the kernel but do not distinguish individual instructions.
FullOpts disables deployment tiering to stabilize code generation; separate tiered-PGO measurements were retained to bound deployment behavior.

The extension host had uncoordinated foreground/background activity. In the 262,144-sample interleaved run, an unchanged Perlin SIMD control shifted from 15.7 to 25.4 ms and OpenSimplex2 SIMD distributions became strongly multimodal. Even fixed-affinity parallel runs had one unstable baseline round. A 3% adoption decision is therefore not robust.

H-010 through H-013 are isolated SIMD screens; their rejected or invalid outcomes were not promoted to complete-API timing. H-014 through H-018 were ruled out by optimized code, table size/dependency, API boundaries, exact-output requirements, or existing scheduler behavior; they are not measured speedup claims.
reproduction: Run raw/run-h001-controlled-caller.ps1 with -Label <name> and optional -FullOpts for complete-caller repetitions.
Run profiling/run-profile.ps1 under the performance lock for EventPipe hotspot evidence.
Run disassembly/run-baseline-disassembly.ps1 under the performance lock for optimized native code.
dotnet test src/Tedd.FastNoise.slnx -c Release --nologo under the performance lock.

For the extension, run git apply --unidiff-zero raw/h009-variant.patch on a clean 99c2c69 checkout, then run raw/run-h009-interleaved.ps1 under the performance lock and reverse only that temporary patch after collecting evidence. The script refuses to compare identical builds.
Run raw/run-h009-h013-mechanisms.ps1 under the performance lock for the five isolated mechanism screens; run raw/run-h009-edge-probe.ps1 with the temporary variant for exceptional-input bit patterns.
